topics.name: Plants and animals on Earth
subtopics: Many different plants and animals live in different habitats; South Africa's indigenous plants, animals and habitats
Interdependence: plants and animals depend on each other and on resources in their habitats
Animal types: invertebrates (no bones) and vertebrates (bones)

topics.name: Animal skeletons
subtopics: A vertebrate skeleton consists of bones and joints inside the body and forms a strong frame
The skeleton supports the body and protects organs: skull, backbone, ribs; limbs and hip bones for movement
Vertebrates move because muscles are attached to the skeleton and there are joints between bones

topics.name: Skeletons as structures
subtopics: A vertebrate skeleton is a frame structure
Some invertebrate skeletons, such as a crab's, are shell structures

topics.name: Food chains
subtopics: Green plants make their own food using water, carbon dioxide and sunlight, releasing oxygen
Animals need food for their life processes and depend on plants as their primary food source (herbivores, carnivores, omnivores)
A food chain shows feeding relationships starting with a plant, and the transfer of energy along the chain

topics.name: Life cycles
subtopics: Plants and animals grow and develop throughout their lives
A life cycle describes the stages of growth and how one generation gives rise to the next through reproduction
Death can occur at any stage; many animals care for their young

topics.name: Metals and non-metals
subtopics: Properties of metals: shiny, hard, strong, malleable, ductile, high melting points; metals are mined from the Earth
Properties of solid non-metals: dull and brittle

topics.name: Uses of metals
subtopics: Metals conduct heat; some are magnetic; only iron rusts, some metals tarnish
Metals are used for coins, wire, jewellery, furniture, buildings, bridges, cars, utensils and roofs

topics.name: Processing materials
subtopics: Materials can be combined to make new materials by mixing and setting (plaster, concrete), mixing (glue paste), mixing and cooking (dough), mixing and cooling (jelly), mixing, drying and firing (clay bricks)
Properties of new materials may differ from those of the starting materials

topics.name: Processed materials
subtopics: Plaster of Paris, concrete, fabrics, ceramics, glass, plastics and paints have special properties
Processed materials are useful because they can be strong, durable, waterproof, fire resistant, colourful or textured

subtopics: Remediation, revision and consolidation of the term's topics

topics.name: Stored energy in fuels
subtopics: Energy is stored in fuels (including food); everyday fuels include coal, wood, petrol, paraffin, gas and candle wax
Burning fuels gives useful heat and light; fuels need heat to ignite and oxygen to keep burning
Safety with fire in our communities

topics.name: Energy and electricity
subtopics: Energy can be stored in cells and batteries; a circuit transfers electrical energy to where it is needed
Mains electricity is transferred from a power station (e.g. coal-fired) in a circuit to our homes and back
Safety precautions when using electricity

topics.name: Energy and movement
subtopics: Stretched or twisted elastic and compressed springs store energy
Releasing elastic or springs gives movement energy

topics.name: Planet Earth
subtopics: The Earth orbits the Sun in about 365 days (a year)
The Earth spins on its axis once in about 24 hours (a day)

topics.name: The surface of the Earth
subtopics: The Earth's crust consists of rocks and soil; soil, air, water and sunlight support life
Soil comes from rocks: rocks, subsoil and topsoil; topsoil forms as rocks break into grains
Soil types: sandy, clayey and loamy; soil contains air, water, dead remains and living organisms
Soil forms very slowly and must be conserved

topics.name: Sedimentary rocks
subtopics: Formation of sedimentary rock: breakdown, transport by wind and water, deposition in layers, compaction and hardening
Sedimentary rocks have visible layers; examples are shale, sandstone and limestone
Uses: limestone to make cement; sandstone and shale in buildings

topics.name: Fossils
subtopics: Fossils are remains of ancient plants and animals preserved in sedimentary rock and are a record of the history of life
Body fossils (teeth, bones, shells, leaves, seeds) and trace fossils (footprints, nests, eggs, droppings)
South Africa's rich fossil record: the Coelacanth, African dinosaurs and the Cradle of Humankind
